gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.reason: All three panels are rights-blocked upstream, so the collage is an internal proof only. Release needs each upstream rights question decided.

questions.question: The collage can only be released if all three panels are cleared: XTRA-11 (Internet Archive capture of INVOICE-IT, no license: fair-use/commentary rationale, permission, or cut), XTRA-12-RQ1 (do Microsoft's screenshot guidelines cover this documentation figure, including its use in a collage with other screenshots?), and the XTRA-13 R14 question (permission request to the karenware.com operator, a recorded fair-use decision, or cut). If any panel is cut, the collage must be recomposed with a substitute or as two panels; do you want that fallback prepared?

The script frames the collage as real-world VB applications by 'people with problems' who were not programmers (War/SCRIPT.md:742, cue at 744). XTRA-12 is not that: it is a form generated by the VB6 Data Object Wizard and shown with sample data in Microsoft's own documentation. Is a Microsoft documentation sample acceptable as the 'data entry' panel, or should the project look for a user-built VB data-entry app (the upstream search found none with documented VB provenance; the VB3 Data Access Guide scan is borrow-only)? More broadly, none of the three panels is documented as made by an accountant, teacher or small-business owner (XTRA-11 is publisher shareware, XTRA-13 is by a magazine columnist). Keep the narration as illustrative color over these examples, or soften it?

The narration's setting is VB's early years, but the pictures are a 2016 emulator capture of a 1993 program (its Date field shows 02-27-2016), a December 1998 VB6 documentation figure, and a 2003 Windows XP capture of a 1999 VB6 utility (status bar 9/3/2003). No caption dates them. Are these acceptable under that paragraph, or should the edit avoid lingering where the in-image dates are legible (for example, prefer the collage over the focus variants)?

On-screen credits: (a) XTRA-11's credit drops the software year ('Eastern Digital Resources, 1993') on screen to avoid implying a 1993 capture. Accept, or restore the year in the video description only? (b) XTRA-13's credit is still 'proposed, not approved' upstream. (c) The Microsoft statement is shown as instructed, but it is accurate only if XTRA-12-RQ1 is accepted; if not, the line must come off. (d) Should per-panel credits stay burned into the picture, or move to the description, keeping only the Microsoft statement on screen, which the guidelines require?

In the three-up collage, each screenshot is only about 1.0–1.3x its native size (the widest panel sets the common height), so the finest UI text is small at 720p; see qa.md for what stays readable. The optional focus variants enlarge one panel to about 1.7–2x. Use the collage as a brief hold and cut to focus variants while the narration names each kind of program, or hold only the collage?

gates.title: Popularity, installed base, prices, and real VB applications
gates.evidence: The reconstruction uses XTRA-11 (INVOICE-IT for Windows) as the on-screen application. XTRA-11's VB provenance is documented via the publisher's own RELEASE.TXT and HELP.TXT files (Visual Basic 2.0, VBRUN200.DLL). However, the source script at line 691 refers to 'VB6 applications', while the actual documented provenance is VB 2.0, not VB6. The VB identification is supported independently of gray controls (by the publisher's documentation), but it is VB 2.0, not VB6.
